clue.text: Tiny insect with tiny head

parts.note: a midge is a small biting fly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the second 'tiny' gives only its opening letter

explanation.surface: A minute bug with a minute head.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes something much smaller than normal, like a miniature version.

clue.text: Line on chart is round sandbank

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
a bar is a ridge of sand across a river mouth or harbour

explanation.surface: A line drawn on a map turns out to be a circular shoal.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather map draws lines joining places of equal atmospheric pressure, which is exactly this term.

clue.text: Mammoth one-night stand supported by old clown

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supported by another sits on top of it

parts.note: a gig is a single performance by a band
antic is an old word for a buffoon or clown

explanation.surface: A huge woolly mammoth does one show propped up by an ancient jester.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, mammoth means huge or enormous, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Tramline could come to this

indicators.note: the letters of the word tramline could be rearranged to arrive at a new word

explanation.surface: A tram route could end up at the depot at the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging TRAMLINE gives the answer, and the whole clue is also its definition: a tram line runs to a final stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramline runs to its end station, the last stop where the route finishes.

clue.text: Remark that's critical of sport and cricketer

parts.note: a sport, like a brick, is a good-natured, dependable person
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A comment disparaging a game and one of its players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a game but is the old phrase for a good sort, as in 'be a sport'; 'brick' means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is literally a missile and figuratively a hostile comment or piece of criticism.

clue.text: Only child has swallowed humbug

indicators.note: the word for the child takes the other piece inside it, as if eating it

parts.note: a boy is a male child
lone means only or sole, as in a lone survivor

explanation.surface: An only child has gulped down a striped mint sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humbug' is also a British boiled mint sweet, which suits the swallowing picture; here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nonsense or empty talk intended to deceive.

clue.text: Agatha's turn on the snow

definitions.meaning: the crime novelist Agatha, creator of Poirot
in skiing, a ... is a turn made with the skis parallel

explanation.surface: A famous lady takes a turn on the ski slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the detective writer Agatha; the other is a skiing turn named after Christiania, old Oslo.

clue.text: Herbert's original name for co religionists

indicators.note: original in the sense of novel or creative, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Herbert's first name was given to fellow worshippers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' looks like 'first', but it signals an anagram of HERBERT, giving BRETHRE, then N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a religious fellowship call each other brothers, using this old plural.

clue.text: Dr. Doolittle presumably could get down to business

definitions.text: Dr. Doolittle presumably could get down to business

parts.words: Dr. Doolittle presumably could get down to business
parts.note: the doctor of children's fiction speaks to animals, so he could literally chat with a festive bird; the phrase also means start serious negotiation

explanation.surface: The animal-talking doctor could probably settle down to work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to speak frankly and negotiate seriously, getting down to business.

clue.text: Inferior lines the Spanish used on fishing boat

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: a dogger is a two-masted Dutch fishing vessel
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Poor verse written in Spanish aboard a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is crude, badly made verse, so inferior lines of poetry.

clue.text: Trial run included in old agreement

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the others, enclosed by them

parts.note: a deal is a bargain or agreement
R stands for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A test run is written into an old contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a painful experience or test of endurance; historically, a trial by ordeal.

clue.text: Second-rate cooler

definitions.meaning: literally less warm, a temperature that has dropped

explanation.surface: Something mediocre that is also less warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for disappointing or mediocre and also literally means less warm.

clue.text: No recent changes in furnishing fabric

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes, being rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Nothing new has happened in the soft furnishings department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' reads as a noun, but it is the anagram signal for NO RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton cloth used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Make rude gesture when fellows are round a corner

indicators.note: the fellows go round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: cock is an old familiar term for a man or chap
a nook is a small corner or recess

explanation.surface: Lads gathered round a street corner make offensive signs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cocks around A gives COCKAS; NOOK follows. The answer is the British idiom for thumbing one's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes putting a thumb to the nose with fingers spread, a gesture of contempt.

clue.text: Whistle used to summon pet?

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
to call is to summon

explanation.surface: A whistle someone uses to call their pet home.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval, from a crowd for example.

clue.text: Story-books attributed to leading journalist with a gift

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
ed is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Novels credited to a newspaper chief who has real flair.
explanation.definitionFit: A gifted person has natural ability, so is skilled in that way.

clue.text: A friend holding — being in favour — very favourable opinion

indicators.note: the word for the friend holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
pro means for or in favour

explanation.surface: A friend who supports something gives it their warm backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is a positive judgement, thinking well of someone or something.

clue.text: Guerilla making a mess of kitchen

indicators.note: disordering the letters as one would a messy room, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter trashes the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chetniks were Serbian guerrilla fighters, notably in the Second World War.

clue.text: Put at a disadvantage, I pass hat around

indicators.note: the pass and hat pieces go around the single letter

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
a cap is a type of hat

explanation.surface: Someone down on their luck passes a hat round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I pass hat around' pictures someone collecting coins in a hat, but 'around' is the container signal: the pass and the hat enclose I.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap someone is to hamper them so they are disadvantaged.

clue.text: Driver of animals taking the pet horses out

indicators.note: the horses are taken out of the combined letters

parts.note: a hamster is a small pet rodent
H is slang for heroin, called horse, so horses are two H's

explanation.surface: A carter takes the family pet when his horses are let out.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus HAMSTER gives THEHAMSTER; 'out' removes both H's, one for each horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a teamster drove a team of draught animals, before the word passed to lorry drivers.

clue.text: One who is doubtful about dispensing with one hundred royal staff

indicators.note: the doubter does without some letters, which are replaced by the piece placed beside them

parts.note: a sceptic doubts claims
I is one and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A doubter is wary of getting rid of a hundred royal attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: In SCEPTIC, IC (one, hundred) is dropped and RE (about) put in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is an ornamental rod carried by a monarch as a symbol of sovereignty.

clue.text: It takes a long time to swallow a medicinal herb

indicators.note: the long time takes in the letter, as if eating it

parts.note: a century, a hundred years, is a long time

explanation.surface: Taking a herbal remedy takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaury is a plant of the gentian family, traditionally used as a bitter herbal remedy.

clue.text: Difficulty with most of ridiculous directions

parts.note: a rub is a snag or difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is dropped, keeping most of it

parts.note: 'that's rich' means that is ridiculous

explanation.surface: Struggling with most of a set of absurd instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' gives RICH, as in 'that's rich!'; 'most of' drops its last letter to leave RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of instructions, as at the top of an exam paper or in a service book.

clue.text: In a coach — always the cheapest way to travel

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is a poetic shortening of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Going by coach is forever the budget option.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced accommodation on a passenger ship.

clue.text: Notes new variety of avocet

indicators.note: a new variety is a different form, so the letters take another order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher logs a new kind of wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a run of eight musical notes spanning a scale.

clue.text: Uncommunicative pet turns before I do

indicators.note: the word for the pet turns round, reading backwards

parts.note: a cat is a common pet
a turn is a performance, something one does on stage

explanation.surface: A quiet pet takes its turn before I take mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says little and is reserved, so silent in manner.

clue.text: Delicate item of clothing

definitions.meaning: handled with great care or tact
a soft leather glove made from young goatskin

explanation.surface: A dainty garment.
explanation.definitionFit: As a modifier it means gentle and tactful; as a noun it is a glove of fine goatskin leather.

clue.text: Illegal publication that's good and strong

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good
racy means strong or lively in flavour

explanation.surface: A banned book that is both virtuous and spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy includes the unauthorised reproduction of copyright works.
